title: Fix F3 (per-book account uniqueness) and F4 (atomic, idempotent repayments)
statusReason: Statically verified only: syntax, 22/22 static tests, boundary scan, call-site audit, migration ordering review. Includes an additive schema change and an index swap, and the DB-level tests (22 ledger + 2 due-rule) plus typecheck/build have not been run: no Postgres, pnpm or node_modules here. PASS requires the Replit run listed under nextSafeStep, and migration 122 applied before deploy.

commit.workingTree: Uncommitted; bound by content via fin-provenance-manifest.json.

schemaChanges.change: UNIQUE(user_id, code) on finance_accounts replaced by UNIQUE(user_id, book_id, code) (create new, then drop old). In-code: lib/schema-migrations.ts after the book_id ALTER and backfill. SQL: migrations/122_*.sql.
schemaChanges.reversible: Recreate the old index only if no user has more than one book (or duplicate codes across books).

schemaChanges.change: finance_repayments.idempotency_key TEXT NULL plus partial UNIQUE(entry_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL. Additive. Drizzle schema updated (lib/db/src/schema/finance.ts).
schemaChanges.reversible: Drop the index and column; no data depends on them until clients send keys.

behaviorChanges: applyPrincipalRepayment returns number | null (null when the entry does not exist; previously 0). Only caller was the repayments route, now replaced by recordRepayment.
amount and status are updated in one SQL statement.

POST /finance/entries/:id/repayments: repayment row and balance/interest change are one transaction; accepts Idempotency-Key header or body.idempotencyKey (<=200 chars); replay returns 200 with Idempotent-Replayed: true; key reuse with different parameters returns 409; a deleted entry returns 404 (was 201). Without a key behavior is unchanged. idempotency key is not returned in responses.
A user's second and later books can now be seeded with system accounts.
deploymentNotes: Apply migration 122 (or let the boot-time MIGRATIONS run) BEFORE this code serves traffic: Drizzle now selects and inserts finance_repayments.idempotency_key, so a database without the column fails every repayment read and write.
The new accounts index is created before the old one is dropped; both are idempotent.
reviewCatches: The new accounts index was first placed before the book_id column exists (fresh database would fail); moved after the ALTER and backfill.
applyPrincipalRepayment now returns number | null, which would break strict typing of two sort comparators in tests; both fixed.
The SQL runner for the isolated test schema ignores DROP INDEX; the old CREATE UNIQUE INDEX statement was therefore removed from the list so the test schema never gets the old index.

commands.result: one caller of applyPrincipalRepayment (replaced); readers: repayments GET (key stripped), late-fee cron SUM (unaffected); writers: 3 other inserts keep working because the new column is nullable

notRun: pnpm typecheck / build (drizzle types for onConflictDoNothing, transaction return type, new schema column)
pnpm test:finance-db (22 ledger tests incl. recordRepayment suite, 2 due-rule tests, the pre-existing 7)
Applying migration 122 to a copy of production data (index creation, drop)
Authenticated HTTP test of the repayments route (replay header, 409, 404)
openFollowUps: F6 installment pay and payment-agreement verify repeat the non-atomic repayment sequence
Clients must start sending Idempotency-Key for the duplicate protection to take effect
nextSafeStep: In Replit: apply migrations to a staging/test copy, then pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server typecheck, build, test:finance-static, test:finance-db; send the output. If green, FIN-WP-1-FIXES, FIN-WP-1-FIXES-2 and WP-1a become PASS.
